summary.text: Clarence Lam is a Democratic member of the Maryland State Senate from District 12 who has served since January 2019 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A physician in preventive medicine at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, he previously served in the House of Delegates from 2015 to 2019.

paragraphs.text: Lam was born in Allentown, Pennsylvania, and earned a bachelor's degree in political science and biology from Case Western Reserve University in 2003, a medical degree from the University of Maryland School of Medicine in 2008, and a master's degree in public health from the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health in 2011.

He was a legislative assistant to Delegate Dan Morhaim from 2009 to 2013, and he has worked as a preventive medicine physician at the Bloomberg School since 2009 and as program director of its Preventive Medicine Residency Program since 2014.
Lam served in the House of Delegates from 2015 to 2019 and was first elected to the Senate in 2018, taking office on January 9, 2019.
He serves on the Finance Committee, is Senate chair of the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee, and chairs the Senate Howard County Delegation.

From 2019 to 2023 he sat on the Education, Health, and Environmental Affairs Committee, where he chaired the Environment Subcommittee, and he chaired the Maryland Legislative Asian-American and Pacific Islander Caucus in 2021 and 2022.
He advanced from the Democratic primary on June 23, 2026.
